findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles simultaneously
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). A user who is only an admin (not owner) or only an owner (not admin) fails the check, so the intended team-admin/owner permission is effectively limited to users who hold both roles. Should be ||.

findings.title: Calendar update uses booking with stale attendees and never includes new guests
findings.body: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) passes the pre-update booking object, while evt.attendees was built from the updated attendee list. Calendar event references/attendee sync depends on the original booking; the mismatch can cause calendar updates to be inconsistent or fail. Also the error from updateCalendarAttendees is not caught, so a calendar failure after the DB write returns an error even though guests were already added.

findings.title: Guest creation not atomic with duplicate check; duplicate attendees possible
findings.body: The filter for existing attendees uses a snapshot read, then createMany inserts. Concurrent requests or case differences in emails can insert duplicate attendee rows for the same booking. No uniqueness enforcement or case-insensitive comparison is applied.

findings.title: Blacklist check compares unnormalized guest email
findings.body: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased, but guest emails are compared as-is (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A guest entered as 'Spam@Example.com' bypasses the blacklist. Attendee duplicate check is also case-sensitive.

findings.title: Email send failures silently swallowed with no logging of error
findings.body: The catch block logs a fixed string and discards the error object, so failures in sending add-guest emails are invisible in diagnostics. Also the handler reports success even when notifications failed.

findings.title: Emails sent to all guests in input, not only newly added ones
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) receives the raw input guests, including those filtered out as duplicates or blacklisted, and the attendee mapping then treats them as 'new'. Previously existing attendees could receive 'new guests added' emails, and blacklisted addresses can get notified. Should pass uniqueGuests.

findings.title: Booking lookup not scoped and permission checks leak existence
findings.body: The booking is fetched by id without any restriction before authorization; the not-found error and forbidden error differ, letting any authenticated user enumerate booking ids. Also the attendee-permission path lets any attendee add guests to the booking, which is broader than the UI intent.

findings.title: EventManager constructed with the requesting user instead of the organizer
findings.body: new EventManager({...user, credentials}) uses the session user's credentials and destinationCalendar, but when an admin or attendee performs the action the calendar update should use the booking organizer's credentials. Calendar events may be updated through the wrong account.

findings.title: Attendees who are existing guests receive wrong email template
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to attendees whose email is in newGuests, and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail to all others. This is inverted relative to the intent of notifying existing attendees about new guests, and the new guests get a scheduled-booking email with no 'guests added' context.

findings.title: Missing blank line and inconsistent formatting between exported functions
findings.body: New exported function sendAddGuestsEmails is placed directly after the previous closing brace without a blank line, unlike surrounding code; the same occurs before sendFeedbackEmail.

findings.title: Organizer email subject uses first attendee name, not the guest context
findings.body: name is set to this.calEvent.attendees[0].name, which may be an empty string for guests added without names (guests are created with name ''), producing subjects like 'Guests Added: X with  at ...'. Also replyTo exposes all attendee emails.

findings.title: Guest attendees created with empty name
findings.body: Guests are created with name "", and the email subject/greeting relies on attendee names. Emails and the UI will show blank names; this is not validated or documented.

findings.title: Zod schema recreated each render and error message mapping is wrong
findings.body: The schema is redefined inside the component on every render. More importantly, onError shows `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which passes server message keys through t and prefixes error codes into user-facing text; the fallback `|| t('unable_to_add_guests')` is unreachable because the template string is never empty.

findings.title: Validation error shown is generic and stays set after success
findings.body: isInvalidEmail is only reset when cancel is clicked, not on successful add or on subsequent valid input, so the uniqueness/validity error persists incorrectly.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text not translated
findings.body: Tooltip content "Remove email" is a literal string instead of t(...), breaking localisation for the rest of the dialog.

findings.title: Translation key 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' message is misleading
findings.body: The message 'Emails must be unique and valid' is used both for client validation and as the server error code key, and the server's BAD_REQUEST when all guests are duplicates or blacklisted reuses it, giving a misleading reason.
